newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kohl says Germany will reach EMU goals in 1997, 98.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says Germany will reach EMU goals in 1997, 98.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that he was certain that Germany would meet the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union this year and next.
Kohl told German television channel Pro-7 in an interview, "I have no doubt whatsoever that we will reach the criteria in both 1997 and 1998."

Germany, along with many other European states, is finding severe problems in meeting the fiscal criteria for entry to monetary union, which call for a country's deficit to be no more than three percent of its gross domestic product.
Kohl, warning other parties against taking an anti-European stance in the elections next year, said in the interview, "We will beat all those who are against Europe."

Gerhard Schroeder, a leader in the opposition social democrat party, has said repeatedly that he would favour a delay in the start of EMU, planned for 1999, if Germany and other major countries did not meet the entry criteria.
Countries wishing to enter EMU in the first round must meet economic targets on public deficits and debts, interest and exchange rates and inflation to qualify for entry.
